Total collapse of a second provincial/regional bridge over the Maisoncle stream in Valsavarenche (Aosta. Valle d'Aosta) on 23 June 2002, part of the same intense summer rainfall event that caused B02.06.05. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Scrivia stream near Arquata Scrivia (Alessandria. Piemonte) on 26 November 2002, triggered by autumn flooding. The Scrivia is a major Apennine tributary of the Po flowing through the Alessandria province; Arquata Scrivia lies at the foot of the Appennines where the Scrivia enters the plain. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the provincial road bridge over the Trigno river connecting Montenero di Bisaccia (Campobasso. Molise) with San Salvo (Chieti, Abruzzo) on 25 January 2003 at 12:58, triggered by the catastrophic flooding of the Trigno during a violent three-day alluvione. The fifth pier gave way in front of a crowd of onlookers, cutting the main road connection between Molise and Abruzzo for months. A temporary bailey bridge was opened in June 2003 as an emergency measure but suffered repeated flooding closures. Reconstruction began in December 2005 following prolonged bureaucratic delays between the provinces of Campobasso and Chieti. The new permanent bridge was inaugurated in December 2006. No fatalities or injuries were reported from this collapse. The same bridge structure collapsed again during the April 2026 Molise flood event.

Total collapse of the bridge over the Fella river connecting the fraction of Pietratagliata to the SS13 Pontebbana national road near Pontebba (Udine. Friuli-Venezia Giulia) on 29 August 2003, caused by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Val Canale and Canal del Ferro area, with 400mm falling in a few hours — one of the most intense precipitation events ever recorded in the eastern Italian Alps. The collapse isolated the fraction of Pietratagliata for days. The broader event caused 2 deaths (Gerti Schnabl in Ugovizza, Bruno Urli in Malborghetto) and mobilised 2,687 civil protection volunteers. Reconstruction of the bridge and the SS13 access road required 6 years and €13.4 million. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of the Ponte di Cernera on the SP (ex-SP41) in the Contrada Piano di Cernera. territory of Massafra (Taranto, Apulia) on 8 September 2003, caused by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the western Taranto province with 212mm of rain in less than 24 hours at Massafra, 225mm at Castellaneta. The broader event killed two people (Cosimo Filiberto Fanelli and Domenico Quarato) and caused €28 million of damage in Palagiano alone. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific bridge collapse. The bridge was subsequently rebuilt but collapsed again during the October 2005 flood (B05.10.01), requiring a second reconstruction project managed by PPV Consulting.

Total collapse of a national road bridge on the SS16 Adriatica over the Sangro river near Torino di Sangro Marina (Chieti. Abruzzo) on 24 October 2004, triggered by hydraulic forces during intense autumn rainfall causing the Sangro to flood. The Sangro is a major Abruzzese river flowing into the Adriatic Sea; its lower valley is prone to flooding during autumn and winter storms. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a national road bridge over the Taloro river near Nuoro (Sardinia) on 8 December 2004. triggered by hydraulic forces during the severe autumn flooding that struck central Sardinia. The Taloro is a major tributary of the Tirso in the Nuoro province, known for powerful floods. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Ponte Chiavalir on the SR552 (Strada Regionale 552 del Passo Rest) over the torrente Vielia at Tramonti di Sopra (Pordenone. Friuli-Venezia Giulia) on 15 December 2004 at approximately 10:00, during a static load test (collaudo statico) one hour before the official commissioning ceremony. Three trucks loaded with gravel were placed on the 30-metre span to verify its structural capacity; the bridge bent into a V-shape and all three trucks fell into the Vielia stream. Driver Angelo Picotto (75, Mortegliano) was trapped in his cab and sustained non-serious injuries; the other two drivers escaped. Expert investigation attributed the collapse to missing bolts and irregularities in construction execution. In December 2011, the Cassazione confirmed convictions for 4 of 6 defendants: designer Michele Artusato (1 year), site manager Franco Fusciello (8 months), builders Walter Ortolan and Domenico Bruno (1 year 4 months), and surveyor Vigilio Ciriani (1 year). The DB lists municipality as Tramonti di Sotto — corrected to Tramonti di Sopra based on all sources.

Partial collapse of the new bridge on the SP98 provincial road over the Rio Sinigo near Sinigo (Merano. Bolzano, Trentino-Alto Adige) on 10 May 2004, caused by design and construction defects. The structure — a 125-metre prestressed concrete box girder (cassone monocellulare) with post-tensioned cables — failed spontaneously without any external trigger during or shortly after construction. The collapse was cited in a national technical survey as a case study of errors in construction and absence of systematic inspection. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a national road bridge over the Oglio river on the SS42 del Tonale e della Mendola near Capo di Ponte (Brescia. Lombardy) on 27 June 2005. One person was killed and four were injured when the bridge structure failed. The collapse was attributed to design and construction defects. Capo di Ponte is a municipality in Val Camonica whose name derives from its historical position at the head of a bridge over the Oglio river; the SS42 is the main valley artery connecting the Brescia plain with the Alpine passes. The Procura di Brescia opened an investigation.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over a valley (gravina) in the municipality of Massafra (Taranto. Apulia) on 8 October 2005, triggered by hydraulic forces during the intense autumn rainfall that struck the Taranto area. Massafra is known for its deep gravina ravine system. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the bridge on the SP184 provincial road over a dry riverbed near Cassano delle Murge (Bari. Apulia) on the night of 23 October 2005, triggered by the catastrophic rainfall event (equivalent to Apulia's entire annual average falling in three hours) that struck the Bari province. Five people were killed when their vehicles crossed or were near the bridge as it gave way. Two additional people were injured. The collapse occurred the night before the Eurostar 9410 train derailment (24 October 2005, 35 injured), both caused by the same exceptional meteorological event described by Protezione Civile president Guido Bertolaso as an 'exceptional climate event.' A car was also swept into the sea in Bari city during the same event, killing one more person. The broader event caused at least 7 deaths across Apulia.

Total collapse of the bridge on the SP21 provincial road near Adelfia (Bari. Apulia) on 23 October 2005, triggered by the same catastrophic rainfall event that destroyed the Cassano delle Murge bridge and caused the Eurostar 9410 derailment. The collapse flooded many roads and contributed to the isolation of parts of the Bari hinterland. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian overpass over the Turin-Genoa railway line near Villanova d'Asti (Asti. Piemonte) on 15 November 2005. The collapse was spontaneous (triggered=FALSE), caused by design and construction defects rather than an external trigger, and two people were injured. The overpass carried a cycle-pedestrian path over the active railway line. The event prompted RFI and local authorities to inspect similar structures in the Asti province.

Total collapse of a motorway/national road viaduct near Augusta (Siracusa. Sicily) on 24 June 2006, caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle that struck the structure. One person was killed and 14 were injured in the collapse. The event occurred on a valley-crossing viaduct in the Augusta industrial port area. Augusta is a major industrial hub with significant heavy vehicle traffic, and the area has historically been served by the SS114 and the developing A18 corridor. The collapse prompted investigations by the Procura di Siracusa.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge in the urban area over the Crosia stream in Vallecrosia (Imperia. Liguria) on 15 September 2006, triggered by hydraulic forces during intense autumn rainfall. Vallecrosia is a small coastal municipality in the Ponente Ligure where the Crosia is one of several minor streams that periodically flood during autumn storms. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Varaita stream near Frassino (Cuneo. Piemonte) on 28 May 2008, triggered by intense rainfall causing the Varaita to flood. Frassino is a small municipality in the Valle Varaita in the Cuneo Alps. The Varaita is prone to sudden summer floods following intense convective storms. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Stura di Viù stream near Usseglio (Torino. Piemonte) on 29 May 2008, triggered by intense rainfall causing the mountain stream to overflow. Usseglio is a high-altitude municipality in the Valli di Lanzo in the Turin Alps. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of a bridge on the SS195 (or adjacent national road infrastructure) over the Rio San Girolamo at Capoterra (Cagliari. Sardinia) on 22 October 2008, as part of the catastrophic flash flood that struck the coastal area. The event caused 4 deaths: Speranza Sollai (drowned in her home), Licia Zucca and Antonello Porcu (swept away while driving near Poggio dei Pini), and Annarita Lepori (overwhelmed by the Rio San Girolamo in spate). The expert appointed by the court stated that 106 mm fell in 30 minutes — possibly the largest flash flood in Italian history. The judicial investigation charged 8 people including the ex-mayor of Capoterra, ex-ANAS directors (accused specifically of failing to demolish an obstructing bridge on the Rio San Girolamo which contributed to the overflow), and Genio Civile/Protezione Civile officials. All were acquitted in first degree (2017) and on appeal (2020). Reconstruction of the collapsed bridge infrastructure began in January 2021.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Rio Cadula e Ardali near Triei (Ogliastra. Sardinia) on 27 November 2008, triggered by severe autumn rainfall that struck eastern Sardinia. Triei is a small municipality in the Barbagia di Seulo area of Ogliastra. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio Corongiu near Tertenia (Ogliastra. Sardinia) on 22 October 2008, triggered by the same extreme rainfall event that struck the Cagliari and Ogliastra areas on that date (part of the catastrophic Capoterra flood system). No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio sa Minda near Orosei (Nuoro. Sardinia) on 30 November 2008, triggered by severe autumn rainfall. Orosei is a coastal municipality in the Nuoro province facing the Gulf of Orosei. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Savuto river near Nocera Terinese (Catanzaro. Calabria) on 12 December 2008, triggered by intense winter rainfall causing the Savuto to flood. The Savuto valley in the Catanzaro-Cosenza border area is prone to hydraulic damage during winter storms. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Marro stream near Taurianova (Reggio Calabria. Calabria) on 13 January 2009, triggered by intense winter rainfall causing the stream to overflow. The Marro valley is chronically flood-prone. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a viaduct on the panoramic provincial road of Enna (Sicily) on 1 February 2009. triggered by hydraulic phenomena during intense winter rainfall. This is a distinct event from a similar collapse on the same road in March 2015. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Ponte di Fossa. a 35-metre three-span continuous reinforced concrete bridge on the SR261 over the Aterno river providing access to the village of Fossa (L'Aquila, Abruzzo) during the M6.3 earthquake of 6 April 2009 at 03:32. Post-earthquake structural surveys revealed the bridge columns had been severely weakened by prior corrosion: steel bars were extensively exposed through thin covering concrete well before the earthquake. The seismic shaking caused failure of the already compromised columns. Fossa itself was among the most severely damaged municipalities, with most residential buildings destroyed. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse (the broader earthquake caused 309 deaths).

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Aterno river in L'Aquila (Abruzzo) on 6 April 2009 during the M6.3 earthquake. Infrastructure damage to bridges and roads across the L'Aquila valley was a significant element of the overall disaster. which caused 309 deaths. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Partial collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Raio river near Scoppito (L'Aquila. Abruzzo) on 6 April 2009 during the M6.3 earthquake. Scoppito, located northwest of L'Aquila near the epicentral zone, suffered significant structural damage to buildings and infrastructure. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a northern span of the Ponte della Via Emilia (SS9) over the Po river between San Rocco al Porto (Lodi) and Piacenza on 30 April 2009. triggered by the exceptional flooding of the Po during a major rainfall event that raised river levels by over 6 metres. A bridge pillar failed, causing the northern carriageway deck — carrying four vehicles at the moment of collapse — to sink into the river. By a miracle no one was killed; three automobilists were injured. The 1949 reinforced concrete bridge, approximately 1 kilometre long, had been carrying Via Emilia traffic for 60 years and was a key link between Emilia-Romagna and Lombardy. A judicial investigation into culpable collapse charged five ANAS directors; all were acquitted in January 2015 for insufficient evidence.

Total collapse of a viaduct span on the SS626 national road near Gela (Caltanissetta. Sicily) on 21 May 2009. With collapse=TC and triggered=FALSE, the failure was spontaneous, attributed to design and construction defects rather than an external trigger. Three people sustained injuries in the incident. The SS626 corridor in Sicily has been repeatedly affected by viaduct failures (cf. Viadotto Verdura 2013, Viadotto Petrulla 2014) attributable to the poor quality of 1970s–80s construction on geologically unstable terrain.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Dragone stream near Palagano (Modena. Emilia-Romagna) on 31 December 2009, triggered by hydraulic forces during intense end-of-year rainfall. Palagano is a mountain municipality in the northern Apennines where the Dragone stream flows. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the railway bridge over the Corace river on the Ferrovia Cosenza-Catanzaro Lido (FCL. ex Calabro-Lucane) between the stations of Cicala and San Pietro Apostolo (Catanzaro, Calabria) on 28 January 2010, triggered by the flooding of the Corace during exceptional winter rainfall. One fatality was recorded: a maintenance worker of the Ventura company was swept away by the floodwaters at the bridge site. Only the prompt intervention of the train driver, who braked before reaching the collapsed section, prevented a catastrophic rail accident. The FCL line was suspended and remained closed until 4 August 2011 — a closure of 18 months. The structure replaced a previous masonry bridge that had already collapsed in the 1970s and was known to be vulnerable to the notoriously powerful flash floods of the Corace.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Simeri river near Simeri Crichi (Catanzaro. Calabria) on 10 March 2010, triggered by hydraulic forces during the intense winter rainfall that caused widespread flooding across the Catanzaro province. The Simeri river, flowing through the Catanzaro hinterland towards the Ionian coast, frequently floods during intense rainfall events. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Tanaro river near Monchiero (Cuneo. Piemonte) on 27 June 2010, triggered by the flooding of the Tanaro during intense summer rainfall. The Tanaro, flowing through the Langhe wine region, is prone to sudden summer floods. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the municipal bridge over the Dolo stream near Frassinoro (Modena. Emilia-Romagna) on 31 October 2010, triggered by the flooding of the Dolo during intense autumn rainfall. The collapse cut the road link between Frassinoro and the neighbouring commune of Villa Minozzo (Reggio Emilia), isolating communities on both banks. Local authorities demonstrated exceptional efficiency: the replacement bridge was designed and built in just four months, with one month for design and three for construction, and was inaugurated on 20 November 2011. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial bridge near Corinaldo (Marche) on 31 January 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Cesano river. No fatalities or injuries were reported.
Partial collapse of a national bridge near Calciano (Matera) on 1st March 2011 triggered by hydraulic phenomena. No fatalities or injuries were reported

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Corropoli (Abruzzo) on 1 March 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Vibrata river. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial bridge near Campli (Abruzzo) on 1 March 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Salinello river. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial bridge near Colbuccaro (Marche) on 3 March 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Fiastra river. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a national road bridge near Caltagirone (Sicily) on 5 September 2011 associated with severe structural deficiencies and instability phenomena affecting the structure over the Margi stream. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Ponte della Colombiera. a provincial reinforced concrete bridge over the Magra river near the river mouth at Ameglia (La Spezia, Liguria) at 22:05 on 25 October 2011, during the catastrophic alluvione dello Spezzino e della Lunigiana. The collapse occurred when a yacht and a river barge, dismoored by the surging Magra flood, were swept by the current against the bridge piers, destroying the central span under their combined weight. The event was the fourth flood to hit Ameglia in three years. The broader alluvione, caused by 542mm of rain

Total collapse of the Ponte di Stradano. a municipal reinforced concrete bridge with piers in the river bed over the Magra river at Aulla (Massa-Carrara, Tuscany) on 25 October 2011, caused by the catastrophic Magra flood during the alluvione dello Spezzino e della Lunigiana. Aulla was the most severely damaged municipality: the Magra broke its banks, inundating the city centre to a depth of four metres. The collapse was subsequently described as 'annunciato' (foreseeable) given the piers' exposure in the river bed. The Regione Toscana approved a €9.75 million project to replace it with a 195-metre cable-stayed bridge (campata centrale 139m) — the first of the three bridges destroyed that day for which reconstruction tender proceedings were launched (July 2014). The broader event caused 13 deaths and €1.5 billion damage. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a provincial reinforced concrete bridge over the Mangiola stream near Aulla (Massa-Carrara. Tuscany) on 25 October 2011, caused by the catastrophic flooding of the Mangiola — a minor left-bank tributary of the Magra — during the alluvione dello Spezzino e della Lunigiana. The Mangiola, which flows from the Apennine hills north of Aulla, overflowed violently during the 542mm/6h rainfall event. The broader event caused 13 deaths and €1.5 billion of damage across the Spezzino and Lunigiana. The Regione Toscana reconstruction programme included this bridge alongside the Ponte di Stradano and the Castagnetoli bridge. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.
Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Castagnetoli (Tuscany) on 25 October 2011 during the Liguria-Tuscany flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Pignone (Liguria) on 25 October 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding during the Liguria-Tuscany storm event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial bridge near Rocchetta di Vara (Liguria) on 25 October 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding during the Liguria-Tuscany flood disaster. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Brugnato (Liguria) on 25 October 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding during the Liguria-Tuscany storm event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.
Partial collapse and severe hydraulic damage of a municipal bridge near Pontremoli (Tuscany) on 25 October 2011 during the Liguria-Tuscany flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a national bridge near Torre Pellice (Piemonte) on 6 November 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Pellice river. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial bridge near Amato (Calabria) on 22 November 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Cancello stream. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial bridge near Barcellona Pozzo di Gotto (Sicily) on 22 November 2011 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Longano stream during an extreme rainfall event. The event caused three fatalities.

Total collapse of a national road bridge near Sericciolo (Tuscany) on 11 November 2012 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding and scour processes affecting the Aulella stream during an intense rainfall event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Mel (Veneto) on 11 November 2012 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Terche stream during an extreme rainfall event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge near Marsciano (Umbria) on 12 November 2012 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding of the Alliana river. The event caused three fatalities after vehicles were swept away during the collapse.

Total collapse of a provincial bridge near Gallina (Tuscany) on 12 November 2012 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with flooding of the Orcia river during an extreme rainfall event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a portion of the Viadotto Verdura on the SS115 Sud Occidentale Sicula national road near Ribera (Agrigento. Sicily) on 2 February 2013, triggered by a landslide caused by exceptional rainfall that had saturated the slope adjacent to a bridge pillar. The structure, built in the 1960s and found to be compliant with regulations of the time, had no prior recorded structural deficiencies. The expert investigation concluded in 2020 that the collapse was solely attributable to the extraordinary meteorological event and that no human error or maintenance deficiency was responsible. A new viaduct was built and inaugurated in 2020. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Rosola stream near Zocca (Modena. Emilia-Romagna) on 23 March 2013, triggered by hydraulic forces during spring rainfall. Zocca is a mountain municipality in the northern Apennines where streams flood rapidly during rainfall events. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian overpass over the SS5 Via Tiburtina near Rome (Lazio) on 26 September 2013. caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle with an oversized load that struck the underside of the bridge while travelling on the road below. No fatalities or injuries were reported as the bridge was unoccupied at the time. The event prompted closure of the Via Tiburtina and structural assessment of adjacent structures.

Total collapse of the Ponte di Carasco over the torrente Sturla (Valfontanabuona. Genova, Liguria) on 22 October 2013 during a violent flash flood (nubifragio) that struck the Fontanabuona valley. Two people died — Gino Gattorna (68) and Claudio Rosasco (45), both from Moconesi — whose car was swept into the flooded Sturla as the bridge collapsed while they were crossing. The bridge was a 55-metre national road crossing on the SP 225 Fontanabuona. One further person was injured. Subsequent judicial proceedings saw 4 employees of the former Provincia di Genova charged with culpable homicide and culpable collapse (allegedly prolonged failure to carry out scheduled inspections); they were acquitted in May 2017. The bridge was rebuilt in exceptional time — completed in 6 months — and reopened in April 2014.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Diaterna stream near Firenzuola (Firenze. Tuscany) on 24 October 2013, triggered by hydraulic forces during the same autumn rainfall event that caused the Carasco collapse. The Diaterna is a minor mountain stream in the Apennines north of Florence. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Padrongianus river near Olbia (Sassari. Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, triggered by the catastrophic flooding caused by Ciclone Cleopatra — which dropped 440 mm in a few hours, killing 19 people across Sardinia and causing €660 million of damage. Olbia suffered 9 deaths. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of the Ponte di Oloè on the SP46 provincial road between Oliena and Dorgali (Nuoro. Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, caused by the catastrophic flooding of the Cedrino river during Ciclone Cleopatra. Inspector Luca Tanzi (40), a police officer responding to the emergency with three colleagues escorting an ambulance, was killed when the bridge spalletta collapsed suddenly at approximately 18:30, plunging his Land Rover into the void. His three colleagues survived. The bridge was placed under judicial sequestration; subsequent works were found to use substandard materials. A 30-person trial for culpable homicide and disastro colposo was opened; a second trial addressed the fraudulent reconstruction. The bridge was not reopened for over 10 years.

Total collapse of a section of the SP38 provincial road at Monte Pino near Olbia (Sassari. Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, caused by a voragine (sinkhole/collapse) triggered by the catastrophic flooding of the Rio Badu Pinasu stream during Ciclone Cleopatra. Three people died: Bruno Fiore, his wife Sebastiana Brundu, and his consuocera Maria Loriga, who were travelling on the road when a large section gave way. The collapse created a monument to 'inefficiency' — the road remained unrepaired for years. Three people were convicted by the Tribunale di Tempio Pausania in March 2022 for culpable collapse and culpable homicide.

Total collapse of a second provincial/regional bridge over the Cedrino river near Oliena (Nuoro. Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, caused by Ciclone Cleopatra. This was a separate crossing from the Ponte di Oloè on the SP46; its collapse contributed to the complete isolation of the Oliena-Dorgali area. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio Sologo near Galatelli (Nuoro. Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, triggered by the extreme flooding caused by Ciclone Cleopatra. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Rio Enas near Olbia (Sassari. Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, caused by the catastrophic flooding during Ciclone Cleopatra. Olbia, as the epicentre of the disaster with 9 deaths, suffered the destruction of multiple bridges and road infrastructure. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Topino river near Foligno (Perugia. Umbria) on 19 November 2013, triggered by hydraulic forces during autumn flooding. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Aso river near Rubbianello (Fermo. Marche) on 2 December 2013, triggered by hydraulic forces during autumn rainfall. No fatalities or injuries were reported.
Partial collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Miscano river near Apice (Benevento. Campania) on 2 December 2013, triggered by hydraulic forces. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Serina stream near Costa di Serina (Bergamo. Lombardy) on 2 December 2013, triggered by a landslide during intense rainfall. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of the Viadotto Navicelli. a moveable road bridge on the FiPiLi superstrada at Calambrone (Pisa, Tuscany) crossing the Canale dei Navicelli, on 23 April 2014 at approximately 11:00. During a closing manoeuvre after allowing a sailing vessel to pass, a series of bridge components fell onto the roadway below, causing panic among motorists. The collapse was caused by the failure of bolts holding the moveable span. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The bridge, managed by Società Navicelli, is a vital link between the Pisa and Livorno nautical industrial districts; its closure severely disrupted operations for dozens of nautical firms. Repairs required at least one month and two cranes. Confindustria noted that an analogous collapse had occurred at the same bridge in 2014 when a further event occurred in 2026.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Ete Morto river near Sant'Elpidio a Mare (Fermo. Marche) on 3 May 2014, triggered by hydraulic forces during a flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a span of the Viadotto Petrulla on the SS626 national road in the contrada Petrulla. territory of Licata (Agrigento, Sicily) on 7 July 2014. The bridge deck collapsed downward from a height of approximately 4 metres due to sudden failure of the prestressed concrete carrying beams, splintering at mid-span. Two vehicles were involved in the incident: four people sustained minor injuries, including a pregnant woman who was airlifted to hospital in Caltanissetta as a precaution. ANAS immediately established an internal investigation commission. The Procura di Agrigento opened a criminal investigation. The event was subsequently cited by CNR-ITC as a significant example of prestressed concrete failure in Italian bridge infrastructure, comparable to the later Fossano (2017) collapse.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the SS3 Via Flaminia national road near Rome (Lazio) on 24 July 2014. caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle with an oversized load that struck the underside of the bridge while travelling on the road below. No fatalities or injuries were reported as the bridge was unoccupied at the time. The collapse interrupted the SS3 Via Flaminia and prompted closure for structural assessment of similar structures in the area.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Aupa stream near Moggio Udinese (Udine. Friuli-Venezia Giulia) on 13 August 2014, caused by hydraulic forces during a summer flood event. The Aupa is a mountain stream in the Carnia Alps known for flash flooding following intense summer storms. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Santerno river near Casalfiumanese (Bologna. Emilia-Romagna) on 20 September 2014, triggered by hydraulic forces during autumn flooding. The Santerno, flowing from the Apennines through the Imola area, is prone to flash flooding in autumn. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Baganza stream in Parma (Emilia-Romagna) on 13 October 2014. triggered by the flooding of the Baganza during the major rainfall event that struck the Parma area. The Baganza, a tributary of the Parma torrent, overflowed its banks causing significant infrastructure damage. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Rio Ciliegio near Trasta. a fraction of Genova (Liguria) on 10 November 2014, triggered by the major flash flood that struck the Genova area — the second catastrophic alluvione in three years after the deadly 2011 event. The Rio Ciliegio is a minor stream in the Genova hinterland that overflowed during the event, which caused 1 death and widespread infrastructure damage across the city. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Bevera stream near Ventimiglia (Imperia. Liguria) on 15 November 2014, caused by the extreme hydraulic event that struck the Liguria di Ponente. Ventimiglia and the Bevera valley were severely affected by flooding during the November 2014 Liguria rainfall events. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Staffora stream at Salice Terme. fraction of Godiasco Salice Terme (Pavia, Lombardy) on 16 November 2014, caused by flooding of the Staffora during the November 2014 northern Italy rainfall event. The Staffora, flowing through the Oltrepò Pavese, overflowed causing infrastructure damage in the Pavia area. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Viadotto Scorciavacche on the SS189 Palermo-Agrigento expressway near Mezzojuso (Palermo. Sicily) on 30 December 2014, exactly seven days after its inauguration. The viaduct had been opened without the required structural testing and certification (collaudo), with ANAS having moved the inauguration forward by three months. The structure, built on unstable terrain, failed within a week of opening to traffic. The collapse was a major national scandal: Prime Minister Matteo Renzi expressed public outrage; the Procura di Termini Imerese opened an investigation for attentato alla sicurezza dei trasporti and falso, indicting the ex-ANAS president Pietro Ciucci and several ANAS directors. After years of procedural battles, most charges were declared prescribed in 2023; in January 2025 the remaining defendants were acquitted. No fatalities or injuries were reported as the viaduct failed without vehicles in transit.

Partial collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Cerami river near Cerami (Enna. Sicily) on 14 March 2015, caused by structural deterioration in the absence of adequate maintenance. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Cerami has a notable medieval arch bridge of the XII century over the Cerami river, but this event relates to a separate structure in the same area. Limited documentation available for this specific event.

Total collapse of approach span no. 13 (Reggio Calabria side) of the Viadotto Italia on the A3/A2 del Mediterraneo motorway between Laino Borgo and Mormanno (Cosenza. Calabria) on 2 March 2015 at approximately 17:00, during demolition works as part of the Macrolotto 3.2 motorway widening programme. The steel span, found to lack fixings on both supports, slid off pier 12 and fell approximately 80 metres into the Lao gorge below. One worker — Adrian Ionel Miholca, 25, Romanian national of Nitrex Srl — was carried down with the span and died on impact. The Procura di Castrovillari sequestered the entire viaduct; the A3 between Laino Borgo and Mormanno remained closed for several months, effectively isolating Calabria from the rest of Italy along the main north-south motorway axis. ANAS established an internal inquiry commission. The Viadotto Italia, designed with consultancy of Riccardo Morandi and inaugurated in 1969, was at the time the highest bridge in Italy (240m above the valley floor) and had been Europe's highest until 2004.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge on the panoramic road of Enna (Sicily) on 28 March 2015. triggered by hydraulic phenomena during spring rainfall. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Enna's hilly terrain makes the provincial road network particularly vulnerable to hydraulic and landslide events during the rainy season.

Total collapse and severe deformation of the Himera motorway viaduct near Scillato (Sicily) on 10 April 2015 caused by a large landslide affecting the foundation area and surrounding slope. The event interrupted a major motorway connection in Sicily without causing fatalities or injuries.

Total collapse of a national road bridge over the Trebbia river near Bobbio (Piacenza. Emilia-Romagna) on 14 September 2015, triggered by the severe flooding of the Trebbia during intense late-summer rainfall. The Trebbia is known for its powerful flash floods in the upper valley. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The medieval Ponte Gobbo (humpback bridge), a symbol of Bobbio, survived the event despite heavy flooding around it; the collapsed structure was a modern RC road bridge.

Total collapse of the Ponte Tammarecchia on the SP ex-SS 625 between Campolattaro and Circello (Benevento. Campania) on 15 October 2015, triggered by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Sannio region — one of the most severe hydraulic events ever recorded in the province. The masonry pillar was swept away by the Tammarecchia river in full spate, isolating the Alto Tammaro area and cutting off several communities. One of 5 bridges in Circello alone destroyed in the event. The Esercito Italiano deployed Bailey bridge technology; a provisional crossing was installed within months. A permanent replacement bridge (€950,000) was inaugurated in 2018. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Tammarecchia river near Morcone (Benevento. Campania) on 15 October 2015, during the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Sannio region. The bridge was one of multiple structures destroyed on the same waterway during the event, which caused €1.1 billion of total damage across the province. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of the Ponte Jenga on SP109 over the Jenga stream between Campoli Monte Taburno and Cautano (Benevento. Campania) on 15 October 2015, triggered by the catastrophic Benevento flood event. The Provincia di Benevento approved a reconstruction project of €950,000 for the new bridge. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of the bridge on SP95 (Malepara) over the Alente river connecting Casalduni with the SS88 (Benevento. Campania) on 15 October 2015, during the catastrophic Sannio flood event. Casalduni was left completely isolated, without water and electricity, following the collapse. The Esercito Italiano deployed Bailey bridge technology for emergency access. Reconstruction project approved for €570,000. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Cervaro stream near Baselice (Benevento. Campania) on 19 October 2015, triggered by hydraulic phenomena associated with the continuing effects of the October 2015 Sannio flood event. Baselice was among the municipalities damaged during the emergency in which the Esercito Italiano intervened. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the northbound carriageway of the Ponte Allaro on the SS106 Jonica national road near Marina di Caulonia (Reggio Calabria. Calabria) on 1 November 2015, during the major flood that struck the Locride area (the 'alluvione della Locride', 31 October–2 November 2015). The Allaro river overwhelmed the bridge, causing the collapse of the 'ponte monarchico' (the older of the two parallel structures). The remaining partial structure was demolished on 6 November 2015 for safety reasons. ANAS appaltò reconstruction works of €2.5 million in December 2016; the new bridge was opened in December 2020. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific bridge collapse (though the broader flood claimed multiple victims in the area).

Partial collapse of the Viadotto Marrazzita on the SP2 'Saurina' at km 4+100 near Stigliano (Matera. Basilicata) on 18 March 2016, caused by intense rainfall that saturated the roadway embankment and caused the voiding of material around a bridge abutment, opening a large sinkhole. The Provincia di Matera issued emergency ordinance n.21/2016 closing the SP2. TOTAL E&P S.p.A. funded emergency repair works; the bridge was reopened within approximately two weeks. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the torrente Rio in the Macchialaccavone locality of Trivento (Campobasso. Molise) on 10 September 2016, caused by an exceptional flash flood that struck the area following a violent thunderstorm. The collapse isolated several contrade including Casale San Felice, Querciapiana and Montagna, and interrupted the provincial road connecting Trivento to Campobasso for several hours. The Vigili del fuoco and Protezione Civile intervened with pumps. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Annone overpass over the SS36 near Lecco on 28 October 2016 triggered by the transit of an overweight heavy transport vehicle. The collapse caused one fatality and multiple injuries. interrupting a major road connection in northern Italy.

Total collapse of the bridge over the torrente Bruzzano on the SP65 provincial road at Bruzzano Zeffirio (Reggio Calabria. Calabria) on 18 November 2016, caused by renewed rainfall that brought down the surviving half-span of the bridge already severely damaged by the 31 October–2 November 2015 alluvione della Locride. The structure had been closed to traffic since the 2015 event. No fatalities or injuries were reported as the bridge was already interdicted. The 2016 collapse was total, completing the destruction begun a year earlier. Provincial technicians immediately began precautionary checks on an adjacent bridge.

Total collapse of the Ponte delle Fucine over the Bormida river at Murialdo (Savona. Liguria) on the afternoon of 24 November 2016, during the major flood event that struck Piemonte and Liguria (21-25 November 2016) with rainfall comparable to the 1994 alluvione del Piemonte. The Bormida flood sheared off the bridge span, isolating approximately 40 families in the borgate Conradi and Pallareto. The mayor declared the situation 'dramatic'; a temporary ford was installed as an emergency measure. The event prompted significant debate on bridge hydraulic design standards, as the old bridge had zero freeboard against the 200-year flood. A new 57-metre single-span steel bridge was inaugurated in October 2021 after €1.76 million of Regione Liguria funding.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Po river near Sanfront (Cuneo. Piemonte) on 24 November 2016, triggered by the exceptional flooding of the Po during the major November 2016 Piemonte flood event. Rainfall at Piaggia (CN) exceeded 632 mm total during the event, and the Po at its upper valley sections reached extremely high levels. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio Bevera near Monesi di Triora (Imperia. Liguria) on 24 November 2016, triggered by a landslide associated with the extreme rainfall event that struck the Liguria di Ponente — particularly the Valle Arroscia and upper Val Bormida areas, where accumulations reached 349 mm in 24 hours at Pieve di Teco. The Monesi di Triora area is in the upper Tanaro basin and was severely affected by the event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Tanaro river near Priola (Cuneo. Piemonte) on 25 November 2016, triggered by the extreme flooding of the upper Tanaro during the major November 2016 Piemonte flood event. Tanaro levels at Garessio reached 4.88 metres, described as comparable to the catastrophic 1994 alluvione. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of the Ponte Allaro on the SS106 Jonica national road near Caulonia Marina (Reggio Calabria. Calabria) on 23 January 2017, during a severe rainfall event that caused the Allaro river to flood. Two bridge spans on the carriageway already closed to traffic since the November 2015 flood (which had caused partial collapse of the original 'monarchico' bridge) gave way completely. ANAS had already contracted reconstruction works worth 2.5 million euros in December 2016. The SS106 remained closed in both directions. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The new bridge was finally rebuilt and reopened in December 2020 after five years of closures.

Total collapse of bridge no. 167 on the A14 motorway at km 235+800 near Camerano (Ancona. Marche) on 9 March 2017 at approximately 13:30, during lifting operations as part of the construction of a third motorway lane. The temporary support structure failed, causing the bridge span to fall onto the open motorway carriageway below. Two people died — Emidio Diomede (60) and Antonella Viviani (54) from Spinetoli (Ascoli Piceno) — whose car was crushed by the falling deck while travelling towards the hospital; three Romanian construction workers were injured. The judicial investigation involved 22 individuals and four companies (Autostrade per l'Italia, Spea Engineering, Pavimental and Delabech), with charges of culpable homicide, culpable collapse and workplace safety violations. The MIT appointed an independent inspection commission. The engineering expert appointed by the prosecution concluded that risks had been systematically underestimated in both the design and execution phases.

Total collapse of a ramp (asta di svincolo per Marene) of the Fossano ring road on the SS231 'di Santa Vittoria' at km 61.300 near Fossano (Cuneo. Piemonte) on 18 April 2017 at approximately 15:00, involving the sudden failure of a campata without prior structural warning signs. A Carabinieri vehicle was destroyed under the collapsed structure, but the two officers — hearing structural creaking — escaped on foot moments before the collapse. No injuries. ANAS immediately commissioned an internal inquiry led by a Carabinieri general and two structural engineers; initial technical assessments pointed to 'vizi costruttivi' (construction defects) as the probable cause, as the collapse was judged anomalously sudden for a 1990s structure not under significant load. Eight people were subsequently placed under investigation by the Procura di Cuneo for culpable collapse.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Chiusella stream near Strambino (Torino. Piemonte) on 15 June 2017, caused by hydraulic forces during a flood event. The Chiusella and its confluence with the Dora Baltea near Strambino is a recurrently flood-prone area with a documented history of bridge and infrastructure damage. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the municipal bridge at the mouth of the Chioma stream near Quercianella (Livorno. Tuscany) on 10 September 2017, triggered by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Livorno area — causing 8 deaths and destroying multiple bridges and infrastructure after 250 mm of rain fell in approximately 2 hours. The Chioma stream, normally reduced to a rivulet in summer, overflowed dramatically and destroyed the bridge connecting the road to the Chioma Beach residence and marina, isolating residents. A rescue operation was mounted by the Vigili del fuoco and Protezione Civile. The bridge was rebuilt by the Comune di Rosignano Marittimo within approximately 7 months and reopened in June 2018.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Rio Maggiore in the Limoncino locality of Livorno (Tuscany) on 10 September 2017. triggered by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Livorno area. The Rio Maggiore, partially culverted through the city, overflowed catastrophically and destroyed the bridge on the road connecting Limoncino to Valle Benedetta, isolating hillside residential areas. The Regione Toscana, in collaboration with RFI (Rete Ferroviaria Italiana), rebuilt the bridge in approximately two weeks using railway bridge technology, reopening it on 26 September 2017 — one of the fastest bridge reconstructions ever recorded in Italy after a flood.

Total collapse of the Ponte Stefano Gioia over the Lao river near Laino Castello (Cosenza. Calabria) on 7 December 2017 at approximately 14:45. The bridge, a 70-metre glued laminated timber (glulam) structure built in 2000 by the Consorzio di Bonifica del Pollino and considered innovative at the time of its inauguration, had been closed to traffic since October 2017 due to detected structural deterioration. The collapse was attributed to complete lack of maintenance since construction, with fungal growth and wood rot having weakened the primary structural elements. The bridge connected the Campicello fraction of Laino Castello with the Nuppolara contrada of Papasidero near the Grotta del Romito, and was named after a rafting guide from Laino Borgo who died in Chile in 2010. No fatalities or injuries were reported as the structure was already closed.

Partial collapse (severe structural damage requiring full demolition and rebuilding) of the SP 24 overpass connecting Montirone and Poncarale over the A21 motorway near Brescia (Lombardy) on 2 January 2018. caused by a catastrophic fire ignited when a fuel tanker exploded following a chain-collision on the A21 below the bridge. Temperatures reaching 600°C severely damaged the RC beams of the entire bridge span. Six people died in the road accident itself. Structural surveys revealed concrete cores were irreparably compromised; the overpass was demolished in April 2018 and fully rebuilt by Autovia Padana, reopening in September 2019 after over 20 months of closure.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Montone river in Forlì (Emilia-Romagna) on 2 February 2018. caused by hydraulic forces during a flood event. The Montone river, which runs through the Forlì urban park area, has a history of flooding events that have caused repeated infrastructure damage. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Mazaro dry riverbed near Salemi (Trapani. Sicily) on 8 February 2018, triggered by exceptional rainfall that caused the normally dry Mazaro riverbed to fill rapidly. Winter storms in western Sicily in February 2018 caused widespread hydraulic damage. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Polcevera Viaduct (Morandi Bridge) in Genoa on 14 August 2018. involving multiple spans and causing 43 fatalities and 11 injuries. The collapse occurred without a clearly identifiable external trigger and is generally associated with structural deterioration and maintenance-related deficiencies.

Total collapse of an overpass along the A14 motorway interchange in Bologna on 6 August 2018 following a tanker truck explosion and intense fire. The collapse caused severe disruption to the motorway network. Casualties associated with the explosion event are not directly attributed to the structural collapse in the present database.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Rio Coccodi near Uta (Cagliari. Sardinia) on 10 October 2018, triggered by the extreme flood that struck the Cagliari hinterland following 250 mm of rainfall in 24 hours. The same event caused the collapse of the SS195 bridge at Capoterra and forced the evacuation of 49 residents from Uta. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Partial collapse of the bridge over the Rio Santa Lucia on the SS195 Sulcitana national road connecting Cagliari to Capoterra and Pula (Sardinia) on 10 October 2018 at approximately 17:30. triggered by the overflow of the Rio Santa Lucia during an extreme rainfall event (250 mm/24h at Capoterra, half the annual average). ANAS had closed the SS195 in the hours prior to the collapse due to a large sinkhole that had opened at the Rumianca jetty area. The collapse cut the national road in two, isolating the Capoterra area. Capoterra was already known for a deadly 2008 flood. The broader event caused 1 fatality and the evacuation of 57 residents from the area. No injuries directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Fersina stream near Fierozzo (Trento. Trentino-Alto Adige) on 28-29 October 2018, triggered by the extreme hydraulic loading of the Tempesta Vaia storm system that struck northeastern Italy with record rainfall and wind gusts exceeding 200 km/h. The Fersina valley was severely affected by flooding and landslides during the storm. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio Piazzina near Stramentizzo (Trento. Trentino-Alto Adige) on 29 October 2018, caused by the extreme hydraulic forces generated by Tempesta Vaia. The Rio Piazzina, a minor tributary in the Val di Fiemme area, was overwhelmed by the record rainfall associated with the storm. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Partial collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Degano stream near Comeglians (Udine. Friuli-Venezia Giulia) on 29-30 October 2018, caused by the Tempesta Vaia storm system. The Carnia region, including Comeglians, was among the most severely affected areas in Friuli, with seven people evacuated and the entire area losing electricity for several days. The Degano river and its tributaries overflowed, damaging or destroying multiple infrastructure elements. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Adda river at Pizzighettone (Cremona. Lombardy) on 30 October 2018, caused by the extreme flooding of the Adda river during the Tempesta Vaia event and its downstream hydrological consequences. The Adda reached exceptionally high levels as snowmelt and intense rainfall from the Alpine catchment propagated downstream. The cycle-pedestrian bridge, which connected the historic walled town of Pizzighettone across the river, was swept away by the floodwaters. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Aviso stream near Cavalese (Trento. Trentino-Alto Adige) on 29-30 October 2018, caused by the Tempesta Vaia storm system. Cavalese, in the Val di Fiemme, was one of the most severely affected municipalities in Trentino during Vaia: the Aviso torrent and its tributaries overwhelmed their banks, destroying infrastructure and isolating communities. The broader Vaia event caused 2 deaths in Trentino and over 500 evacuations across the province. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Partial collapse (severe structural damage requiring full demolition and rebuilding) of the overpass on the SP 32 Novedratese at km 8.890 in Carimate (Como. Lombardy) on 18 March 2019, caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle transporting an excavator with an oversized load that struck the intrados of the bridge while travelling on the underlying via dei Giovi. All RC carrying beams were damaged, with rebar severed along the entire span. The Provincia di Como ordered the immediate total closure of the Novedratese for a minimum of three months and proceeded with demolition and full reconstruction of the bridge deck. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The closure caused severe traffic disruption across the Canturino and Brianza areas for several months.

Total collapse of a viaduct on the SS106 Jonica national road near Cropani (Catanzaro. Calabria) on 30 August 2019, attributed to design and construction defects. The SS106 Jonica is a notoriously accident-prone infrastructure corridor where several structures had been reported in poor condition. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Specific documentation for this individual event is limited in open sources.

Total collapse of the bridge over the Rio Albedosa on the SP 155 (Pratalborato fraction of Capriata d'Orba. Alessandria, Piemonte) during the night of 21-22 October 2019, triggered by an extreme flood following record rainfall (425 mm/24h at Gavi, the highest in 100 years). One fatality was recorded: Fabrizio Torre, 52, a transport driver from Sale, whose vehicle was swept away by floodwaters near the collapsed bridge. His passenger, a Brazilian national, survived by clinging to a tree. The SP 155 — a key link between Novi Ligure and Ovada — remained closed for several months pending construction of a provisional Bailey bridge, which reopened in February 2020.

Total collapse of the northbound carriageway of the Viadotto Madonna del Monte on the A6 Torino-Savona motorway near Savona (Liguria) on 24 November 2019 at approximately 14:05. caused by a landslide of over 15,000 m³ that detached from an adjacent hillside not classified as at-risk in the regional hydrogeological risk maps and struck a bridge pillar, bringing down approximately 20-40 metres of bridge deck. A tragedy was narrowly averted when security guard Daniele Cassol stopped oncoming traffic — including a bus — on the brink of the collapsed section. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The bridge was rebuilt in an extraordinary 88 days by Autostrada dei Fiori and reopened in February 2020, becoming a symbol of rapid infrastructure recovery.

Total collapse of a pedestrian bridge over the Sarno river on via Ripuaria in Castellammare di Stabia (Naples. Campania) on 21 December 2019, triggered by the overflow of the Sarno river during severe rainfall. The bridge, which had reportedly been out of use for some years, was destroyed by the rising river; debris from the collapsed structure threatened to block the river flow. The Campania Protezione Civile confirmed no injuries. Municipal technical staff and the Consorzio Bacino del Sarno were alerted and the Genio Civile coordinated the emergency response.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Gonessa (Sud Sardegna. Sardinia) in April 2020, triggered by overload from a heavy vehicle exceeding the structural load capacity of the bridge. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The structure was a small municipal crossing typical of the rural Sardinian road network.

Total collapse of the Ponte Emilio Barsanti over the Magra river near Albiano Magra (Massa-Carrara. Tuscany) on 8 April 2020, caused by a landslide that undermined the bridge's foundation pier. Two injuries were reported. The bridge, a reinforced concrete structure on the SS330 state road, was a vital link between Tuscany and Liguria. Its sudden collapse during the COVID-19 lockdown drew national attention and accelerated the debate on Italian bridge safety monitoring.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Paglia river near Abbadia San Salvatore (Siena. Tuscany) in May 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena following intense rainfall. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Arrone stream near Santa Maria di Galeria (Rome. Lazio) in September 2020, triggered by overload from a heavy vehicle that exceeded the load capacity of the structure. One injury was reported. The collapse interrupted local road connections in the area northwest of Rome.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Niel stream near Gaby (Aosta. Valle d'Aosta) on 2-3 October 2020, triggered by the extreme flash flood that struck northwestern Italy with record rainfall exceeding 600 mm in 24 hours in some locations. The collapse was explicitly reported by the Valle d'Aosta civil protection authorities during the emergency, isolating the Gaby area. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Cervaro stream near Piedicavallo (Biella. Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, during the catastrophic flood that broke historical rainfall records in Piemonte (610 mm/24h recorded at Piedicavallo itself). No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Partial collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Strona stream near Crevacuore (Biella. Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, caused by the extreme hydraulic loading associated with the October 2020 northwestern Italy flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Ponte Lenzino over the Trebbia river near Piacenza (Emilia-Romagna) on 2-3 October 2020. triggered by the extreme flood that struck the Trebbia valley during the major northwestern Italy rainfall event. The Ponte Lenzino in the Alta Valtrebbia, on the SS45 connecting Piacenza and Genova, was one of three bridges cited in official reports as destroyed during the event. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Sesia river connecting Romagnano Sesia and Gattinara (Novara. Piemonte) on 3 October 2020. The bridge had been closed overnight as a precaution, was briefly reopened when conditions appeared to improve, then collapsed at approximately 13:30 — the collapse was broadcast in near-real time during a Facebook live session by the two mayors. One person died in the Sesia river floods nearby, but not directly from this collapse. The event was widely reported nationally.

Total collapse of the Ponte Manfredi over the Arroscia stream near Vessalico (Imperia. Liguria) during the October 2020 flood event affecting the Ponente Ligure. The collapse was explicitly named in national media coverage of the disaster. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Tanaro river near Bagnasco (Cuneo. Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, triggered by the historic flooding of the Tanaro river which reached record levels in the upper valley. Sources refer to a 'ponte romano' at Bagnasco among the structures destroyed during the event, suggesting a masonry arch structure of historical origin. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Total collapse of the Passerella Squarciafichi cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Roia river in Ventimiglia (Imperia. Liguria) on 2-3 October 2020, caused by the extreme flooding of the Roia river during the October 2020 Ponente Ligure flood event. The structure was described as a symbol of the city. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Gesso stream near Valdieri (Cuneo. Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, caused by the extreme hydraulic loading during the record-breaking October 2020 flood event in the Cuneo Alps. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Strona stream near Valstrona (Verbania. Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, triggered by the extreme flood affecting the Verbano-Cusio-Ossola area where rainfall records were broken (630 mm/24h at Sambughetto). No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian wooden overpass on via Laurentina near Piazzale Ardigò in Rome (Lazio) on 8 October 2020. caused by a crane truck that accidentally struck the underside of the timber bridge while manoeuvring on the road below, splitting the structure in two. The bridge was unoccupied at the time and no injuries were reported. Roma Capitale coordinated restoration works, with the missing span reinstalled in 2021.
Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Mollarino stream near Picinisco (Frosinone. Lazio) on 19 October 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Enel hydroelectric canal near Pallanzeno (Verbania. Piemonte) on 6 November 2020, triggered by the transit of a heavily loaded truck transporting cleaning material for the Rio Valmaggia. The structure may have been weakened by the October 2020 flood. The truck remained suspended on the collapsed bridge overnight; the driver was unharmed. Enel, owner of the canal, undertook reconstruction of a new permanent bridge inaugurated in 2024.

Partial collapse of a national bridge over the Neto river near Crotone (Calabria) in November 2020. triggered by hydraulic phenomena following intense rainfall. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio de Malò near Bitti (Nuoro. Sardinia) in November 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena associated with severe rainfall affecting central Sardinia. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Panaro river near Pavullo nel Frignano (Modena. Emilia-Romagna) in December 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the bascule bridge (ponte levatoio) at the Darsena di Pagliari in La Spezia (Liguria) on 12 May 2021. during a closing manoeuvre after allowing a vessel to exit the marina. The structure, inaugurated in 2010 by the Port Authority at a cost of over 9 million euros as part of the Pagliari marina development, was 21 metres long with a 14-metre mast. No fatalities or injuries were reported, as the area is routinely closed to traffic during bridge operations. The Port Authority immediately sequestered the structure for judicial investigation for alleged culpable collapse.

Total collapse of the bridge over the Logonovo canal along via della Salina near Comacchio (Ferrara. Emilia-Romagna) on 28 August 2021, due to structural deterioration. The collapse isolated the historic Saline di Comacchio — an important tourist and ecological site — and disrupted local mussel farming operations for over a year while reconstruction was planned.

Total collapse of a lateral service gallery of the Ponte dell'Industria (Ponte di Ferro) over the Tevere river in Rome on the night of 2-3 October 2021. triggered by a large fire that started from makeshift encampments beneath the bridge and spread to gas and electrical service conduits running along the structure. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The bridge, built in 1863 and an important connection between the Ostiense and Marconi districts, was reopened to vehicles on 12 December 2021 following emergency repairs.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Quazzola stream in via Tecci near Quiliano (Savona. Total collapse of the Ponte San Bartolomeo on the SS187 state road near Alcamo Marina (Trapani. Total collapse of the Ponte Guastacconcio over the Sangro river near Paglieta (Chieti. Abruzzo) on 13 February 2022. Partial collapse of the Via Volturno overpass over the western ring road (tangenziale Ovest) in Brescia on 24 August 2022. caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle transporting a crane whose boom struck the underside of the bridge deck. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Temporary shoring works involving 250 props were installed and load tests were carried out before partial reopening.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Misa river near Arcevia (Ancona. Marche) on 15 September 2022, triggered by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Marche region. Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Nevola river near Ostra Vetere (Ancona. Marche) on 15 September 2022. Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Bevano stream near Cantiano (Pesaro-Urbino. Marche) on 15 September 2022. Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Acquaviva stream near Arcevia (Ancona. Marche) on 15 September 2022. Arcevia was one of the municipalities most severely affected by the 15 September 2022 Marche flood, sustaining multiple bridge collapses and road interruptions simultaneously.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Sanguerone stream near Monterosso Stazione. fraction of Sassoferrato (Ancona, Marche) on 15 September 2022. Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Sanguerone stream near Sassoferrato (Ancona. Marche) on 15 September 2022. Total collapse of a second municipal bridge over the Sanguerone stream near Sassoferrato (Ancona. Marche) on 15 September 2022, triggered by the same extreme hydraulic event that caused the simultaneous collapse of multiple bridges in the area during the catastrophic Marche regional flood.

Partial collapse of the Cavalcavia XXV Aprile in Novara (Piemonte) on 9 October 2022. involving the detachment of a retaining wall section. Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge on the Paraturo stream near Laino Castello (Cosenza. Calabria) on 17 November 2022, triggered by intense rainfall and consequent hydraulic loading. Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge on the SP329 near Monteverdi Marittimo (Pisa. Tuscany) on the night of 1 December 2022, caused by the sudden failure of a pillar.
